messages.content: Can you help me find public libraries in New York, NY that have a Reading Room and Fiction section, and then in Los Angeles, CA that offer Wi-Fi and have a Children Section, and finally in Chicago, IL that have a Cafe and a Reading Room?

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function multiple times with different parameters. The function signature: public_library_find_nearby takes location (string) and facilities (one of the listed options). But it seems facilities expects one value from union type? Actually it's defined as facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; That means facilities can be either a single string among those or an array of strings? The description says "Facilities and sections in public library." So maybe we pass an array of desired facilities. But the type indicates union: either a single string or an array of strings. We want multiple facilities per query. So we should pass an array of strings.

Thus we will call function three times:

1. location: "New York, NY", facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]
2. location: "Los Angeles, CA", facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"]
3. location: "Chicago, IL", facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"]

We'll produce calls accordingly.
